I reviewed six of the 14 completed inspections from 11/9 to 11/15. The other eight weren't in the results, and I don't have a paging parameter, so I haven't reviewed them yet.

**Urgent: Harbor Eastside Grill (fac 40118830, District 3, scored 41/C, 3 priority violations)**
- Its reinspection was due 2026-10-14 and is still unscheduled, about 32 days overdue.
- Epidemiology linked four salmonella cases to this facility on 9/22. Two people were hospitalized.
- On 10/17, Deputy Commissioner Leon Collman placed the reinspection on "HOLD-EXEC." The emails tie the hold to the facility owner's gala and fundraiser connections and the Commissioner's calendar through 11/30. Collman also directed staff not to post it to the public board. Senior Inspector Naira Ahmed objected in writing on 10/16, saying the file shouldn't be signed off without a visit.

A hold based on a donor relationship rather than public health risk is a serious problem. I've flagged the facility on the schedule, which is logged and visible to oversight. I haven't sent alerts or contacted anyone outside the division, and I haven't changed the hold.

I recommend escalating this now to the Commissioner, the Office of the Inspector General, or the division's ethics or compliance office, whichever applies. Ms. Ahmed's written objection and the 10/17 hold email should go with it. If the cluster is still active, the epi team should also get a same-day reinspection and sampling visit. I can draft an escalation email to any of those contacts if you want one, or send an urgent alert to the supervisors and epi team. I'll wait for your go-ahead on either.
